video_title: Luka Gets Called Out As Lakers Dominate + Who Made A Game 1 Statement?

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Slater on the poor performance of Northern California teams
quotes.excerpt: Northern California did not show up too well.
quotes.quote: All four California teams doing battle like an old-school AAU tournament across the city yesterday. Northern California did not show up too well.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on his long drive between San Antonio and Houston
quotes.excerpt: I made the drive between San Antonio and Houston.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Howdy partners, I actually made the drive between San Antonio and Houston. You know what highway that is, Brian?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Rare decision by MacMahon to drive across Texas, Slater, that is not something we normally see.

text_blocks.speaker: Anthony Slater
text_blocks.text: You know what highway that is? That's like three, three and a half?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Yes, but there was construction, so I had to go these back roads.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on his high-speed drive in a rental car
quotes.excerpt: I took some toll road that I had never taken before and the speed limit was 85.
quotes.quote: During the finals last year, I had to fly into Austin once and I drove from Austin down to San Antonio and I took some toll road that I had never taken before and the speed limit was 85 miles an hour. 85 miles an hour and I had a rental car, which was a German rental car, and that car, despite being German, was not built for speed limits of 85 miles an hour.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Warriors' need for Yaxel Lendenborg's comic relief
quotes.excerpt: I think the Warriors are going to need Yaxel Lendenborg's comic relief during this season.
quotes.quote: I understand that there's going to be a lot of reaction to what Yaxel Lendenborg did, and you were there, Slater, but I think the Warriors are going to need Yaxel Lendenborg's comic relief during this season. That's my assessment after watching them in Game 1.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Slater on the Warriors' dying era and missed opportunities
quotes.excerpt: This is a dying era, right? The Warriors, they know it.
quotes.quote: Let's be plain, this is a dying era, right? The Warriors, they know it. And they've had missteps along the way, which includes the Porzingis situation, which we're going to talk about, or the draft picks of stars they were hoping to get to carry the next era, Wiseman, Kuminga, Moody. And there's been misfortune, the Jimmy Butler ACL tear, I think put them in a really bad spot.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Yaxel Lendenborg's potential and the Warriors' support
quotes.excerpt: Yaxel is probably good for the NBA. You want this.
quotes.quote: First off, let me just say that Yaxel is probably good for the NBA. You want this. And Slater, you wrote a piece on him a couple of weeks ago. The Warriors love this guy. And I say guy because he's not a kid. He is a grown man, he's 24 years old. They love him, and they understand that he is going to go through his growing pains, and they understand that he's going to probably put his foot in his mouth both on the court and maybe to the media.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on Victor Wembanyama's performance against Victor Kessler
quotes.excerpt: They're going to see the anti-Kessler, Victor Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: They're going to see the anti-Kessler, Victor Wembanyama. He starts 0 for 12, Kessler starts 12 for 12.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Walker Kessler's impact on the Lakers' defense
quotes.excerpt: The Warriors got hammered by Walker Kessler on a whole bunch of lobs.
quotes.quote: You have to be careful evaluating who maybe screwed up on defense because NBA defenses are very complex and they're in different coverages and you're not necessarily sure, but the Warriors got hammered by Walker Kessler on a whole bunch of lobs where they totally lost him. And a couple of them were off screens where Kessler came up and set the screen and then rotated to the basket and it was, I think Yaxel was at least partially responsible for some of those lobs.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on Luka Doncic's impact on his teammates
quotes.excerpt: Luka made Derek Lively and Dainu Gaford the best they've ever been.
quotes.quote: Luka made Derek Lively and Dainu Gaford the best they've ever been. Gaford had a crazy run of consecutive made field goals, I think the second longest in NBA history right after he was traded to the Mavericks. Kessler obviously starts 12 of 12, 10 of those are dunks, five of them are spoon-fed by Luka. There's a reason Walker Kessler was willing to walk on glass from Salt Lake City to LA to play with Luka.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Bucks' investigation and Gary Trent
quotes.excerpt: Gary Trent, DNP-CD in the first game of a four-year $64 million deal.
quotes.quote: I don't know if you noticed the Bucks opened the season, just to check in on the other investigation, Gary Trent, DNP-CD in the first game of a four-year $64 million deal. I told you, no need to investigate, pay that entire contract, every single penny of it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Bucks' investigation and the Clippers' deal
quotes.excerpt: If this is proven to be true, then this is actually more egregious than the Clippers' deal.
quotes.quote: I don't know what's going to happen in that investigation. I will tell you that it is a frequent conversation as I talk with people around the league. It is being done by a different law firm than did the Clippers' investigation. An executive said to me that they think, and I want to be clear, I want to be cautious, but an executive say to me if this is proven to be true, then this is actually more egregious than the Clippers' deal.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Warriors' trade inquiries for Porzingis
quotes.excerpt: The Warriors started making calls looking for availability for Porzingis trades.
quotes.quote: The reason this popped up across the NBA landscape was that the Warriors started making calls looking for availability for Porzingis trades. And that all of a sudden popped up on the radar of Shams and others, and that's what happened here.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Slater on Porzingis's health and trade flexibility
quotes.excerpt: He was around the team in the week leading up to training camp.
quotes.quote: He played 15 of the last 20 games last year that had them like decently confident enough that they can maybe maintain his health to provide every other game type support for them this season. He was around the team in the week leading up to training camp. He went to this event with Jimmy Butler in San Diego, but if you talk to the players and people at that event, he wasn't getting on the court, he wasn't in the weight room. He would show up to kind of more of the dinners and the fun stuff, but it seemed clear right before camp that he was fading away from basketball, obviously dealing with his health issue and thinking about his future.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Timberwolves' trade for LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: The Timberwolves' decision to trade for LaMelo Ball has been very interesting.
quotes.quote: A team that made a swing over the summer that I have to say, when I have worked with other former players here in ESPN, this week it's been a Montrezl Harrell, it's been Kendrick Perkins, but just watching the reaction over the summer of what the former players or even some current players think about the Timberwolves' decision to trade for LaMelo Ball has been very interesting. And I've started to say that the Timberwolves are kind of like your favorite player's favorite team.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Chris Finch's quote about the Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: We traded moodiness for giddiness.
quotes.quote: I think that one of the more interesting quotes in the whole preseason came from Chris Finch when he said, we traded moodiness for giddiness. It's a fascinating quote because it's not and he didn't mean Naz Reid as the moodiness, he was talking about Julius Randle.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Rudy Gobert's role in the Timberwolves' offense
quotes.excerpt: Rudy is like grabbing the ball off the rim and heaving it down the court.
quotes.quote: Rudy is like grabbing the ball off the rim and heaving it down the court. He's getting rid of it because he wants to start the break. He wants to get the ball in the hands of LaMelo and Ant obviously.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Blazers' offseason and coaching hire
quotes.excerpt: The Blazers had a lot of offseason angst, largely around their owner.
quotes.quote: The Blazers had a lot of offseason angst, largely around their owner and, you know, the future, the arena situation, the way that the Dunden wants to operate the team, the hiring Mikael Nori on a glorified one-year contract, too many guards, you know, the Ja Morant trade, all of these things.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Andy Miller's new role at Lift Sports Management
quotes.excerpt: Andy is joining Lift Sports Management as a senior executive role as COO.
quotes.quote: Andy is joining Lift Sports Management as a senior executive role as COO, and you will oversee the agency's operations and lead their growth and strategic operations and direction. And so Lift is Mike Miller is the president of Lift, former NBA player, who I've known for many years. Kevin Bradberry is with them, he's been a long-time agent, and Donnie McGrath is I think the CEO.

quotes.speaker: Andy Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Andy Miller on his long career as an NBA agent
quotes.excerpt: I joined the business in 92, if we're being completely honest.
quotes.quote: I joined the business in 92, if we're being completely honest. By 94, I had negotiated a couple of European deals and by 94, 95, I was already negotiating NBA deals. So I've been around a long time to say the least.

quotes.speaker: Andy Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Andy Miller on the trigger point for Kevin Garnett's rookie contract
quotes.excerpt: The trigger point for Garnett's first rookie contract was that there wasn't any restricted free agency.
quotes.quote: The trigger point for Garnett's first rookie contract was that there wasn't any restricted free agency. So there weren't option years, it was three years and then he was free. So the leverage was enormous at that stage. You could lose someone for nothing. At that point, people don't remember, but he was the first threshold of players that weren't getting those big contracts as rookies. The Jason Kidds, the Jermaine O'Neals were getting 50, 60 million dollar deals as lottery picks before they even proven themselves.

quotes.speaker: Andy Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of load management on NBA game outcomes and player roles
quotes.excerpt: the escalation of seriousness of load management and how much it has made an impact on how games are played
quotes.quote: the utilization of the masseuse and the trainer and these other things that are necessary to prepare people for games and the escalation of seriousness of load management and how much it has made an impact on how games are played, who plays in the games and the outcomes of games. When you start to mitigate staffing, you are sending mixed messages not only as an organization but to the players.

quotes.speaker: Andy Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Budenholzer's attempt to recreate his past success in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: he is trying to recreate or create something maybe recreate what he did in the NHL
quotes.quote: I am not rooting for Mike Budenholzer to not have success and Joe Cronin is a general manager and we have done a lot of business together and I respect him immensely. But he is trying to recreate or create something maybe recreate what he did in the NHL, I do not know for a fact, but definitely create something that has not existed in the NBA and we will see what the reaction will be over time.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Budenholzer's lack of playing experience and coaching philosophy
quotes.excerpt: he is not going to sit around and say I will wait for the next job I get
quotes.quote: Mike Budenholzer is, you know, he is not a former player. He did not win like three rings as an assistant. He did not come out of the San Antonio pop school like so many did. He is not going to sit around and say I will wait for the next job I get off the bench. He is not going to take it. So I get that.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: P.J. Carlesimo's advice on coaching success and contract length
quotes.excerpt: for a head coach to be successful in the NBA, you really need to have a lot of years
quotes.quote: I will never forget P.J. Carlesimo. P.J. was at the end of his coaching career really and he got the interim coaching job of the Brooklyn Nets. He replaced Avery Johnson and he had his first press conference as the interim coach. For a head coach to be successful in the NBA, you really need to have a lot of years on your contract and you really need the players to know you have a lot of years on your contract.

quotes.speaker: Andy Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: The offset mechanism in NBA coaching contracts after being fired
quotes.excerpt: there is an offset variable that these coaches do not like to sit out
quotes.quote: Most coaches do not finish their career when they get fired, they move on to the next job. It is a cyclical sort of thing and it goes on in perpetuity. And so there is an offset variable that these coaches do not like to sit out. There is language in contracts which stipulate that you have to try and get a job rather than sit back, kick your feet up on a beach and not work off of whatever owners' dollar.

quotes.speaker: Andy Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: The lack of unionization for NBA coaches compared to players
quotes.excerpt: the difference is that one is a union and one is not
quotes.quote: It is a little bit different because there is a Coaches Association, not a Players Association, in that the difference is that one is a union and one is not. And so the Coaches Association, while they work very hard and Dave Fogel who runs it bleeds the Coaches Association and lives it day in and day out and is completely dedicated to it, the reality is the voice in the room, not his fault, but the voice in the room because it is not unionized, debilitates the ability to carve out certain things or to protect certain areas.
